Priya (oncall): incident-bot triggered paging: P1 - high 95th/99th latency on /v1/generate, errors rising, backend queue depth spiking.
incident-bot: ALERT: P1 - v1/generate high latency - 2156789012 - paging eng-oncall. @Priya (oncall) @Samir
Samir: seeing a huge backlog on the request-queue metric, queue_depth ~ 18k for gpu-pool-a, normal ~500-1k. :alarm:
Priya (oncall): copying logs now, can someone pull latest warmup metrics and HPA events?
infra-ops: attaching last 6 minutes of HPA events and pod lifecycle:
```
2026-03-15T18:20:05Z HPA scale up from 12 to 18 replicas - reason: cpu/utilization
2026-03-15T18:21:10Z pods scheduled but taking >45s to become Ready - warmup timeout
2026-03-15T18:22:00Z HPA attempted further scale to 30 but kube quota throttled
```
Lara: the GPUs are saturated on pool-a, memory pressure -> eviction thrash seen in node logs. Sharing `dmesg` snippet and pod OOM traces.
Samir: hypothesis 1: HPA triggered scale but warmup warmup-seq (model load + KV init) is long, requests queue up -> autoscaler thinks it's still under-provisioned -> backpressure spiral.
Ethan: hypothesis 2: kube throttling due to resource quotas hitting cloud limit, so even though HPA wanted more, controllers couldn't provision nodes quickly.
Priya (oncall): mitigation 1: switch traffic to dedicated fallback model (lower perf but ready) - can we flip routing for customer-facing routes? @infra-ops
infra-ops: applying a routing override now - divert 30% of /v1/generate to model-fallback-1. Command:
```
redwood route update --path /v1/generate --traffic '{"model-primary":70,"model-fallback-1":30}'
```
Samir: patch applied, traffic shift started. Monitoring latency and error-rate.
Priya (oncall): also increasing warmup concurrency: bump warmup parallelism to 8 for pool-a.
infra-ops: warmup concurrency increased, issuing `kubectl patch` now. Note: pods still take ~30s to reach steady-state KV cache.
Lara: adding logs: snippet of request traces showing tail latency spikes at 18:20:40 - 18:23:00, correlated with HPA events.
Samir: current numbers post-mitigation: queue_depth down from 18k -> 7.2k in 2m, p99 latency down from 1.8s to 700ms on fallback-routed requests. Errors reduced.
incident-bot: PAGE_RESOLVED at 2156790200 (partial) - customer impact reduced, continuing monitoring.
Priya (oncall): handoff note for next shift: we think primary chain of events is: sudden traffic spike from a customer job -> GPU pool saturation -> HPA triggered -> node provisioning rate limited by quota -> pods warm up slowly -> requests queued -> autoscaler perceived need grows -> surge.
Ethan: logging pointer: s3://redwood-logs/2026/03/15/cluster/pool-a/trace-2156789.tar.gz
Priya (oncall): action items (short):
 - infra: request temporary quota bump for region-us-west-2 (open ticket #INC-8672)
 - runtime: add pre-warm hooks for model load to reduce ready latency (investigate parallel KV seeding)
 - product: throttle known heavy job patterns or require rate-limit headers
 - oncall: add a quick runbook step to reroute to fallback model if queue_depth > 5k
Samir: adding timeline entry to the thread doc and uploading logs to the RCA drive.
Lara: suggest follow-up postmortem to include heap snapshots and cold-start profiling.
Priya (oncall): ok handing off to @Samir for overnight watch, I'll link to the pagerduty incident and updated tickets. Leaving pinned logs and commands in thread. :white_check_mark:
Samir: acknowledged, I'm monitoring alerts and will escalate if queue_depth > 6k again. Good notes, will run initial RCA draft in morning.
infra-ops: ticket INC-8672 opened with cloud-ops, ETA 2h for quota increase.
Priya (oncall): thanks team. end of handoff.
